summary: Ustaz Azlan resumes the sirah after Ramadan with the moment the Prophet SAW received revelation. He introduces several sirah books, describes the Prophet's SAW family at 40 and his weariness with Makkan society that led him to retreat to Hira. Using Aisha's hadith in Sahih Bukhari, he covers six months of true dreams, the meaning of tahannuth, the difference between a prophet and a messenger, Ibn Qayyim's eight forms of revelation, the date of the Quran's first revelation, Jibril's three embraces, the Prophet's SAW fear, and Khadijah's test to tell an angel from a devil.
keyPoints: At 40 the Prophet SAW had four daughters at home and was devoting time to family and to helping the weak.
Revelation began with six months of true dreams, then he retreated to the Cave of Hira, explained as tahannuth, not asceticism.
A prophet differs from a messenger; the ustaz prefers the view that a prophet continues the law of an earlier messenger.
Ibn Qayyim lists eight forms of revelation, including dreams, inspiration to the heart, an angel in human form, a ringing bell, the angel's true form and direct revelation at the Mi'raj.
On the day of the first revelation Jibril embraced the Prophet SAW three times while commanding 'Read'.
Khadijah RA calmed the Prophet SAW and tested whether the visitor was an angel or a devil.

lessons.title: Read many sirah authors
lessons.body: Reading widely enriches perspective and avoids misunderstanding.

lessons.title: Child safety in vehicles
lessons.body: The ustaz reminds us about seat belts and baby seats.

lessons.title: Time with family is not downtime
lessons.body: Devoting time to children and family is the most important and obligatory phase.

lessons.title: Read sirah to change
lessons.body: Studying religion with no change is only entertainment.

lessons.title: Seek solitude to clear the mind
lessons.body: A short retreat helps separate what matters from what does not.

lessons.title: Tahannuth is not asceticism
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW retreated yet kept engaging with society and did not cut off.

lessons.title: Islam does not kill desire
lessons.body: Ramadan trains desire; worship must not abandon eating, sleeping and family.

lessons.title: Trust the written provision
lessons.body: Provision is like a room with lawful and unlawful doors; we do not die until it is complete.

lessons.title: Know prophet from messenger
lessons.body: A prophet continues the law of an earlier messenger and a messenger brings a new law.

lessons.title: Revelation is protected
lessons.body: Allah promised to preserve the Quran so that no one can change a letter or word.

lessons.title: A spouse's support in crisis
lessons.body: Khadijah stayed calm, encouraged and sought answers when the Prophet SAW was afraid.

lessons.title: This religion begins with reading
lessons.body: The first word is 'read', then pen and writing, not TikTok and WhatsApp.

glossary.meaning: Retreating to leave sin and filth; related to tahannuf and not asceticism.
One who is upright and does not worship idols.
The assembly hall of Makkah's leaders, like a parliament.
From naba' (important news); the recipient of important news who must convey it.
One who brings a new law; the ustaz prefers the view that a prophet continues an earlier messenger's law.
A swift signal, a gift from Allah.
True dreams, the first form of revelation.

dalil.context: Aisha's hadith in Sahih Bukhari, chapter on the start of revelation.
dalil.translation: Revelation began with the true dream; whatever he saw in sleep came like the break of dawn. Then solitude became dear to him and he would retreat to the Cave of Hira.

dalil.context: Six months of dreams equal one forty-third of the 23 years of revelation.
dalil.translation: The true dream is one of forty-six parts of prophethood.

dalil.context: Shows Islam does not teach asceticism.
dalil.translation: Salman spoke the truth; I fast and I eat, I pray at night and I sleep, I marry; whoever turns from my sunnah is not of me.

dalil.context: Taken as a sign that creation had welcomed the time of prophethood.
dalil.translation: I still know a stone in Makkah that greeted me before I was sent; I still know it now.

dalil.context: The companions asked about the beginning of his prophethood.
dalil.translation: I am the answer to my father Ibrahim's prayer and the glad tiding that Jesus brought.

dalil.context: Shows prophets and messengers are not the same.
An example of the second form of revelation: inspiration into the heart without seeing the angel.
dalil.translation: Jibril blew into my heart that no soul will die until its provision is complete, so fear Allah and seek it in a good way.

dalil.context: The fourth form; the Prophet SAW sweated even on a cold night.
dalil.translation: Revelation comes to me like the ringing of a bell; it is the hardest on me, and when it ends I have grasped what was said.

dalil.context: An example of the third form, the angel in the form of a man.
dalil.translation: Jibril came in the form of a man in pure white clothes and asked about Islam, faith and excellence; the Prophet SAW then explained it was Jibril.

dalil.context: Used to compute the date of the Quran's revelation.
dalil.translation: I fast on Monday because I was born that day and revelation was first sent to me that day.

dalil.context: Surah Al-Kawthar came down when the Prophet's SAW son Abdullah died and his uncle cheered 'cut off'. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: We have truly given abundance to you [Prophet]––

dalil.context: It is the Prophet's SAW enemy who is cut off, not him. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: it is the one who hates you who has been cut off.

dalil.context: Allah says the Prophet SAW was searching and was guided. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Did He not find you lost and guide you?

dalil.context: The first embrace of Jibril foreshadowed the weight of the 'heavy word'. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: We shall send a momentous message down to you.

dalil.context: Allah assures the Prophet SAW he will not forget revelation, so do not move the tongue hastily. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: [Prophet], do not rush your tongue in an attempt to hasten [your memorization of] the Revelation:

dalil.context: Affirmation of his exalted character when he feared being possessed like soothsayers and poets. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: truly you have a strong character––

dalil.context: The first word revealed, 'Read'. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Read! In the name of your Lord who created:

dalil.context: After reading, the verse 'Nun. By the pen' mentions the pen. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Nun By the pen! By all they write!
